headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 7 studies yielded an effect size of 1.09 (95% CI: 0.98–1.2), indicating no statistically significant association between processed meat intake and bladder cancer. Although the point estimate suggests a potential positive relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by moderate heterogeneity (I² = 41.86%), suggesting some variability in the results across studies.

design.excerpt: Individual data from 11 prospective cohorts comprising 2848 BC cases and 515,697 non-cases with a total of 5,498,025 person-years of follow-up was pooled and analysed
